question: Should maintainers refresh and land this Codex lane-release replacement with focused runner proof, or require live wedge proof before merge?
rationale: The patch is a plausible best fix for the source-visible lane-release gap, but the current head is conflicted and the remaining choice is maintainer acceptance of session-state overlap and proof sufficiency rather than a narrow code defect.

options.title: Refresh And Accept Focused Proof
options.body: Rebase or recreate the branch on current main, rerun exact-head checks, and accept the focused regression as sufficient for this runner-owned contract.

options.title: Require Live Wedge Proof
options.body: Pause merge until a live or Crabbox Codex app-server wedge shows lane release without session corruption or user-visible delivery loss.

options.title: Pause The Replacement
options.body: Keep or close the replacement if maintainers decide the conflicted branch is not worth carrying forward right now.

recommendation.title: Refresh And Accept Focused Proof
recommendation.body: Rebase or recreate the branch on current main, rerun exact-head checks, and accept the focused regression as sufficient for this runner-owned contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main Codex app-server changes are likely to drive the refresh/conflict resolution and proof-sufficiency decision.
